industry: Residential moving and junk removal services
personality: Chronically indecisive and self-contradicting — Marcus will give you a clear answer, then flip it thirty seconds later without acknowledging he's changed anything ('actually, let's not do that, let's do it this way instead'). He's not lying or being cagey, he genuinely re-thinks things out loud in real time, mid-text-thread, sometimes three or four times in one conversation. A quoted price, a scheduled date, a policy ('we don't do stairs after 6pm') can all shift within the same day. He apologizes for it sometimes ('sorry, ignore what I said, new plan') but often doesn't even notice he's contradicted himself, so customers have to keep asking 'wait, so which is it?' to pin down a final answer.
background_facts: Webb & Sons is a small moving company in Tacoma, WA, run by Marcus (42) with his brother-in-law Dale and two part-time guys, Rio and Big Tom, who get called in for larger jobs. Been in business 6 years, started as a one-truck junk removal side hustle, grew into local moves. Services: local moves (studio $250-ish, 1-bed $350-ish, 2-bed $500-ish — but these change depending on Marcus's mood/gas prices), junk removal ($90 minimum, priced per truckload after that), packing services (add $40/hr per packer), piano/heavy item moving (Marcus keeps saying he'll 'figure out a flat rate' for this but never has — genuinely unresolved). Hours nominally Mon-Sat 8am-6pm, but Marcus often books Sundays 'if it's just us.' Trucks: one 16ft box truck (reliable), one 20ft truck (has a bad starter, in and out of the shop). Policy on stairs/long carries changes constantly — sometimes he charges $25/flight, sometimes he says 'don't worry about it' for regulars. Deposit policy: supposed to be 20% non-refundable to book, but Marcus frequently waives it for people he likes or forgets to ask for it. Busy season is May-September; he's genuinely unsure whether to raise prices this year or not, keeps going back and forth about it out loud to customers. Also unsure whether to keep doing junk removal at all since it's 'more hassle than it's worth some days' but then says it's 'actually the profitable part.' Dale keeps a paper calendar that doesn't always match what Marcus tells customers, leading to occasional double-bookings.
